After that, the normal alcohol and foils were put on my hands before the pedicure. text: Where do I start? We searched for hotels a month or so out from our stay and settled on the Bayfront. While the prices were a bit higher than we wanted to spend, the location and proximity to our event made sense. Boy were we in for a surprise. In short, it was not worth the $$ or location, this is a surprisingly poor Hilton, charging Vinoy like rates. My wife and kids checked in for a two night stay after a long drive on a Friday night (2/21/2020). We made our way into the room and were immediately disappointed. The room's only light was a lamp with no lampshade. Admittedly this doesn't sound so bad until you attempt to rummage around the room with ambient bathroom light or turn on the lamp and try not to create a comedic music video for "blinded by the light". Additionally it appeared as though someone had attempted to melt the toilet seat with a curling iron and had one otherwise pristine white comforter with a subtle yet visible large stain of unknown but suspicious origin. The room was also incredibly outdated and not the "Hilton" standards I am used to. But it was too late to care, so we went to bed. The very next morning, being the loyal Honors member I am, I made my way to the front desk and informed the staff that there was no shade on the lamp and damage to the toilet seat. The informed me that someone from engineering would visit the room and take care of it. I returned to the room to find my children gazing at the bay front view of the adjacent roof and several AC units. After showering and getting ready for the day, we dropped our towels in the tub, left the beds a mess, and took off for a quick jaunt to pick up a relative for the event we were in town for. Upon returning to the room around 3PM we found it had not been touched. No lamp shade, no new towels, no clean linens. I assumed they were busy as there were still housekeepers cleaning rooms. So we took a quick break, got ready for our event and left the room. We returned to the room around 930PM to find... you guessed it, no change. No clean towels, no lamp shade, no clean linens. I promptly retraced my steps and asked the front desk if they still cleaned rooms. Faced with confused and somewhat incredulous faces. Our dirty towels were still in the tub, there was still no lampshade, and our room had not been cleaned. I informed them of our issues and that we were prepared to go down the street to the Vinoy promptly if they could not remedy the situation, at least I know we would have a clean room. The first Hilton employee apologized and informed me I would be getting 1000 points added to my account. (Ironically, this is the exact amount of points you receive if you ELECT to not have your room clean. I do not believe the irony was intentional or noticed.) The other employee informed me that they would send someone to replenish the towels and give the room a quick clean. I informed them both that we would be eating in the lobby and out of the room for the next hour or so. At this point, while we were enjoying tasty flat breads from the restaurant, the second Hilton front desk staffer saw us and comped our entire email and drinks. "OK," I thought, "this is heading in the right direction". Upon entering the room around 1030PM, guess what we found. You got it... no change. No clean towels, no clean linens, unmade beds, dirty towels right where we left them, and still no lamp shade. Now at this stage it was not only too late again to care, but I also realized no amount of complaints will address the issue for the evening. So we turned in for the night, un-showered from our athletic event. The next morning, we promptly woke up, packed, and cleared the room. I approached the front desk to return my key, saw fresh new faces, and pleasantly informed them of our journey. After many apologies and aghast faces I was told that both managers were at the front desk the night before and should have taken care of the issues. Obviously they had not. I then informed the staff that this was my worst stay at a Hilton owned property, that i would be leaving a review, that my family would not be driving back home without showering (did I mention we were at an athletic event?), and that I would not ever grace that property with my loyalty, family, or dollars again. After a round of cordial "have a nice day"s, we promptly left. At this point, we were still willing to concede that it may have been a one off issue, that is until we met another of our group's families in the parking lot. I bet you know where I am going :). They had the same issues, well mostly, they at least had a lamp shade. But you guessed it, their room had not been cleaned, they had also not received any new towels or linens either. Needless to say, I will choose a Motel 6 over this property any day. I would give 0 stars (if i could), but we at least had beds and clean laundry on the first night, at least that is what I keep telling myself.

text: We stopped in after making reservations for an early Saturday evening dinner. Overall, we had good food, generous portions, and a pleasant server. The interior of the restaurant is broken into lots of small rooms and a bar that you can partially see from the entry. There is also a Host lectern that was unmanned, so we waited a couple minutes for anyone of the staff to greet us. I don't understand the point of having a station for a host and not having anyone there. But since we had reservations, someone eventually arrived and seated us to the right in one of the small rooms. We waited a few minutes and our waitress arrived and took our beverage orders. We watched as two other couples arrived and left because no one was there to greet them. Some other people arrived and seated themselves at the bar. It was becoming a pattern of confusion about seating. After our beverages arrive, we quickly placed our orders to make sure the food was put in the queue. Although we never had that long to wait, we rarely saw any staff during the visit because of our secluded room. It felt odd. By mid-meal, we noticed that one of the male servers was telling guests that there was a 30 minute wait. We had a 6-person table in our nook that was unfilled and I could see a 4-person table unused across the way. Did they simply not have enough staff to man the tables? Again, it seemed like a lost revenue opportunity for the restaurant because ALL the customers who were told of the delay left. Fortunately, our food arrived in a timely fashion and it was quite good. I had a starter cup of Guinness Onion Soup that had a delightful flavor. There wasn't any actual broth since their version has garlic bread cubes in the soup that absorbed all the broth. The onions were so cooked that they were there in flavor, but not visible (they must have completely broken down into the broth.) The cheese topping was melted and easy to dig through with a spoon which made eating the soup very easy. Really good flavor. The only real negative was that the house bread was a bit dry and without any broth to dip it in, it was less than I had hoped. I also ordered the fish 'n chips. A large single piece of battered white fish came with lots of seasoned potato wedges, cole slaw, and tartar sauce. Good flavor without being overcooked made for a filling meal. Note that they do have malt vinegar on the tables for those who prefer it to tartar sauce. My wife got the Paddy Mac Sandwich with the corned beef replaced by smoked turkey. It comes with cole slaw on the sandwich along with Swiss cheese, 1000 Island dressing and served on marbled rye and a side of the potato wedges. She thought the flavor was pretty good but though the ratio of turkey to cole slaw was light on the turkey. As I mentioned above, we enjoyed our meal and found our server to be pleasant though some small delays occurred. If you are looking to beat the crowds, you should visit during the weekday! A couple of tips: There are no bathroom pit stops along the way, so if you are planning on going with young children, make sure you do your potty stops beforehand! Also, like I said, it takes about 30 minutes to get through, so plan ahead and bring snacks, water, etc., so that you're not hearing kids complaining about being hungry or thirsty while you're trying to admire the lights. By the way: Don't let my crappy photos deter you. This light show is amazing! text: I highly value programs and internship opportunities that are designed to build character and the value of hard work into college students. I also know that not everyone who participates in such internships has the integrity and self-awareness to know when the door of opportunity has closed and it's time to shove off. Such was the case today. Mike (an eager college student from Poland) came knocking on our door this afternoon. I answered and we chatted a bit and I encouraged him to come back when my wife and daughter were home so that we could all go over the materials he was selling together. Well, he showed at about 7:30pm and rather than the 10 minutes he claimed to need, he spent an hour asking questions and presenting materials. The materials were only average in our opinion (both my wife and I have bachelor's degrees and I have a master's degree in our respective fields) and the cost for the materials was extravagant to say the least. I could hire Albert Einstein and Blase Pascal for less. I had to step away and in the interim he wrapped up his presentation and asked my wife for a yes or no on the spot. She gave him exactly what he asked for... she told Mike we wouldn't be interested and thanked him for coming back. He continued to press and my wife continued to say no... 3 more times. He asked, "Is it the money or do you believe she won't use the materials?" My wife replied, "It doesn't matter why my answer is no... it's no. Thank you for coming." Now, here's the reason I'm writing this review... Mike then proceeds to disengage from my wife by turning to my child and asking her, "Can you promise your mom that you will use the books if your mom buys them for you?" Nope. That level of desperation clothed in sleazy emotional manipulation crossed the line and Mike was politely asked to depart. He will not be permitted to return and we won't be recommending him or Southwestern Advantage. I have been in sales off and on in my life (currently on) and I know when the "party's over"... especially when in someone else's home. Manipulation and high pressure tactics are never effective and always leads to customers having buyer's remorse which then creates more work to either refund the money or justify why you won't. Either way, it's bad for all involved. This is both a personal integrity issue and likely a training issue as well that SW Advantage needs to address in the case of one of their reps for sure and if it's a systemic issue, they need to retune and retrain.

text: I was cordial and polite when I replied to a listing for a dog at LNF. I expressed interest in a particular dog there and explained that I've been a pet lover since I was a child. I've had cats, dogs, fish, rodents, reptiles, even a pet spider in my lifetime, all of which were treated like family members. I expressed my liking that this particular dog was house trained. I mentioned I liked that the dog gets along well with other dogs, and how I liked that it was purebred and already neutered. I also mentioned rescue animals from shelters can be less expensive than professional breeders or even backyard breeders, which I will NEVER deal with. I explained my current cat of four years was a rescue and detailed the veterinarian we use for her needs. I advised that my wife and I had spent a couple weeks discussing the possibility of adopting a rescue, to ensure we were both ready to make this move. And that we both came to the decision we were ready to do this together and give it our 100%. I received a one sentence reply where a woman named Marlene passed her judgment on me, and evidently out of the several paragraphs I typed, only saw the part of my letter that mentioned money. And I assume from that, she took me for some low-life just trying to save a couple bucks by inquiring on a dog at LNF. She couldn't be more wrong if she tried. The other criteria she used for rejecting my application was because I was liked that this dog was a purebred, which I wasn't aware was a crime. And contrary to her assessment of everyone who was denied, my wife and I did read the requirements. We just didn't realize there was anything "sinister" in wanting a purebred dog. The assumption Marlene made that money was the top factor while looking for a pet was just her own mistake while judging people. Everyone who I've shown my note to, and then saw her snippy reply just scratch their head in amazement, wondering how many other good people were written off based on this woman's incorrect analysis of someone. I find it humorous in her own review on here of LNF that she validates her rudeness by claiming it's in response to rudeness directed at her. Again, she couldn't be more wrong if she tried. My initial letter as well as my followup to her nasty reply with an exclamation point at the end, were both polite and cordial. I don't stoop to other people's levels to meet them where they can relate. I will simply share my experience online at every venue I can think of, as well as spread the story by word of mouth to anyone I know who loves animals. Which is a decent amount of people. We have a rescued cat who is healthy, loving and greets all visitors with warmth and love. Because that is what she receives here. This woman Marlene might be patting herself on the back for a job believed to be well done, has not saved a dog from a low-life, money grubbing jerk that just wanted to save 100 bucks. She prevented the dog from joining a family with plenty of time to spend with a pet, a family with a spacious fenced-in back yard to run in, and a family who would have welcomed a new pet as a brand new family member. Do yourself a favor and keep looking at other rescue organizations, where maybe the staff aren't so snooty and feel like they're able to pass judgment on people via the internet, without even meeting them in person to REALLY get to know someone. Sadly, one star is the lowest rating you can give on here. Otherwise I would've given LNF a zero.
label: NEG

text: I live on the island, so I've been coming here casually since it's opened. It's hit or miss for me as far as food is concerned, it is what it is. The location is great. The way its designed and decorated is great... its comfortable inside when its hot as hell outside, outside is great in the 'fall' months, but those misters they installed drench you if you're not careful. Is the food good? Its ok. They've changed their menu once or twice or three times and its down to a handful of decent bar menu items that we all eat. There are some entrees, but this isn't the place I'd come for a business meeting where we eat steaks and chat... I come here for business meetings because we want to drink and be around locals while we chat. It's a casual ambiance. To each their own. They have a good happy hour, from 4-7 Monday through Friday, where you can get apps and drinks for half off. Burger and two drinks is under $14 I think during happy hour which is definitely a decent deal. It's also good for docking your boat to grab food coming/going from either Islands. I've had decent experiences with some, good experiences with others, one or two bad apples like any bar and then one really good experience with someone that I try to see when we come over... Joseph. Met him here few months ago when we were coming a little more frequently. Even where they are slammed, he always acknowledges us when he sees us. I've watched people get a little mouthy with him only for him to just kill them with being professional. His drinks are always onpoint (even if sometimes they could use an extra .5 second pour), but hes always been good to my crew and anyone we bring in there. Runners up? Alyssa. She's always on point and friendly... there were a couple others, but I haven't seen them in awhile nor do I remember their names. If you're in town for a convention or game or concert, def check it out. It can be a lot of fun when the crowd is just right. Sometimes it gets a little too crowded, sometimes it's hot AF outside (and even inside), but its a really good jump off point for you if you wanna pre-game before going out (or when youre done)... ...If you live here, you already know about it so you dont need my review.

Now I wasn't expecting Fourth of July sparkling bottles of Cristal being walked to my table by scantily clad women, but I sort of expected, at least an offer, of something like a complimentary glass of wine. For the amount of money this place rakes in, I just found it really tacky. Although, they were gracious enough to dump confetti on my table. Happy birthday me. Other than the happy birthday confetti, it was no different than being just a regular customer. they actually moved us out of the main dining room closer to the bar per our request. We browsed the menu and after some time made our selection. I ordered the "celebration surf and turf" with 2 cold water lobster tails and an 8 oz. filet mignon per recommendation of the waitress. I ordered my steak 'blue', as per the norm. As we continue to imbibe, with not even so much as an offer of a cheap well drink, our main course comes. Oh, going back to my pictures, I remembered we ordered butterflied shrimp for an appetizer, but it's apparent that they weren't nothing spectacular if I can't really remember without seeing a picture I took of them. Thinking back, they were actually the best thing we had eaten and the entire restaurant that night. Anyhow, getting back to the steak, my steak isn't exactly blue, it's more on the medium well side. Okay. That's fine. I'm hungry, and I'm already basically discouraged and disappointed at this place. So I just stay quiet and eat my steak, patiently awaiting my lobster tails. As I see the waitress make a few trips to tables around our vicinity, I decide to ask her when they will come out. She then tells me that she didn't know I ordered lobster tails with my meal, even though SHE WAS THE ONE WHO SUGGESTED IT. So, I'm basically done with my steak, now I'm waiting for my lobster tails. Notice I said tails, as in plural, as in two. A little bit of time goes by, and here comes A SINGLE LOBSTER TAIL. Me, being gullible and optimistic, only because this is supposed to be a five-star high-class restaurant, I'm guessing my other lobster tail is on its way. I finished my lobster tail, and pull the waitress again and ask her where my other lobster tail is. She then asks me if I want another one. at this point, having been there two hours, I just said F*** it, and said no. We finish gallivanting and drinking our cocktails, and the check comes. Guess how my (not) "surf and turf" meal was broken down? Item-by-item. So instead of paying for a meal that I think was around 60 bucks, it came to about 80, maybe more if I remember right. The actual amount isn't important, it's the fact of the matter that the lack of attention paid to me, especially on my birthday, let alone a regular customer is unacceptable, and breaking down my meal item by item. I don't know if she was new, or if she was just overwhelmed, but I still can't wrap my mind around how you suggest a meal configuration, that I immediately order, and you not only get it wrong, but you bill me as if I ordered all a la carte items! Enough of that, let's get to the food. For all this decades-long praise and positivity about this place, especially amongst entertainers, and high-profile people alike, it sort of makes me wonder if any of these people have ever been somewhere other than Denny's and McDonald's in their life? The steak, like I said, overcooked, but the filet mignon although tender, is the least flavorful cut of steak. Ask a butcher. When I mentioned that to the waitress, she kind of sneered at me. Obviously not knowing who I am or knowing what I know, or knowing how much I cook. Other than that, it was just a filet mignon, nothing special, and definitely DEFINITELY not something I would go back for. Matter of fact, if I ever did go back, which I can probably guarantee you right now I never will, I would never order it again. The lobster tail, was indicative of being cooked in a hurry. And I also noticed as I was waiting on my lobster, other tables were getting theirs. Kind of chewy and rubbery on the ends, but slightly palatable in the center. And I forgot to mention, when I ordered initially I ordered extra lemon and butter, which I didn't get until I was almost finished with it. Now I don't know who made the mistake on my order, whether it was the believably knowledgeable waitress, or the kitchen, but I just know it was wrong, and I am not impressed, and I will not go back to a Ruth's Chris ever again. As a matter of fact, I went to outback for the first time in 15 or 20 years, and their food and service completely blows Ruth's Chris out of the water. So, if you've read this far, and you're considering going, and you haven't been there before, you'll still go, but you'll see. Oh, will you see.

text: From the second we walked in we were greeted in a friendly manner. The whole staff was great, great service, and super helpful when it came to giving suggestions. We got there pretty late, right before 10pm so it was quiet. There were 3 tables total including ours. We ordered hot sour soup, spring rolls, vegetable soup dumplings, fried veg balls, pineapple fried rice, and stir fried ho fun. Everything was great! Hot sour soup is my favorite soup and this place didn't disappoint. My boyfriend had the spring rolls and he said he really enjoyed them. It was our first time eating soup dumplings and the dough "wrapper" was thicker than I thought it would be, but maybe that's just how soup dumplings are to hold in the soup? It was still good though, it was flavorful. The fried veg balls were surprisingly better than I thought they would be. It was perfectly crispy on the outside and a nice doughy consistency inside. The pineapple fried rice was good, but warning it is sweet. They used a sticky rice and the texture was perfect! It also does look exactly like the picture on the menu. Lastly the stir fried ho fun was delicious. I usually get beef chow fun without the beef, so to have a vegetarian version with mushrooms was pretty exciting. I got it without the vegetarian ham so they added more mushrooms in for me! The tea is also worth getting. For $1 a person it was a nice addition to our meal. We both had the jasmine green tea. Overall we enjoyed our dinner here and would definitely recommend/come back! Also last thing to note, we were pretty full afterwards, but this Chinese food didn't make us feel gross like normal Chinese food does.

text: For years I commuted from the suburbs into Center City, and walked by the Rittenhouse Tria (every day), wishing I could go in, but I had a child to take care of at home. Lo and behold, we moved into Washington Square West (when said daughter graduated from HS), and I stumbled upon this location of Tria. I checked out their menu, and reviews, and quickly got excited to try it. Please be advised that this review is being done during the COVID-19 pandemic, so it does NOT include any comments on regular in-house service, or ambience. So, I ordered the fig/prosciutto/Gorgonzola salad, mushroom bruschetta and crab stuffed peppers for my husband; the Mozzarella/prosciutto panino for myself. OK, so, we both LOVED our dishes. I did not know that my panino came with a side salad - very fresh and delish! The panino was gigantic, stuffed with mozzarella, prosciutto, pesto, tomatoes, and grilled to perfection on a lovely bread - could either be shared, OR, in my case, 2 meals - gigantic! The crab stuffed peppers did not sound all that good to my husband, BUT, HE QUICKLY CHANGED HIS MIND AT THE FIRST BITE!!! Fresh lump crabmeat stuffed into red peppers (with a delicious (basil?) sauce. We both tasted the mushroom bruschetta, and (imagine that), we both enjoyed the earthy flavors of the mushrooms (not sure what type they used (still learning my way around mushrooms), but they were not button mushrooms - shiitake, Cremona???), and the smooth, melted fontina was a perfect pairing with them. The salad was right up his alley; he adored and devoured it! We both really enjoyed the prosciutto they use - a little salty, a little sweet - just perfection (obviously imported, which in our opinion is the very best). He is about to go back onto a low/no carb diet, which helped him lose 100 lbs - now he wants to lose 20 more, so he is going NO carb, and this was a last hurrah - for him. I will continue to order from Tria, and when my husband loses his last 20 lbs, he wants to keep going back for more! We can't wait for a vaccine, so we can feel safe eating outdoors in nice weather, and seeing what the indoor space has to offer. Their on-line ordering system was very simple to use. The system did state that it would be 40-45 minutes for pick-up, but I got there early, and expected to wait, but our order was all packed up and ready. The servers at the door asked me to wait for a moment - OK, well, it was REALLY only a moment, while a drink was delivered by one, and a plate delivered by the other. Less than 30 seconds later, I was approached by a very pleasant, smiling young woman, who brought out my order in a matter of 15 seconds. I have long suspected that I would enjoy this place - and I was RIGHT!!!!

I heard new roads would get built to streamline getting in and out of the airport, so maybe this will help, but I think that's a few years away. Limited seating... text: WHAT AN EXPERIENCE. Tailer Nashville exceeded all of my expectations. the customer service, the chef, the host - all of the above. This place felt cultural and progressive at the same time. I love how the chef introduced himself at the beginning and every meal related to a story. He also explained all of the dishes really well. All of the ingredients were fresh, and all the dishes were served to everyone together. The restaurant did a fantastic job of catering to all dietary restrictions and did fantastic work at bringing the REAL taste of India and merging it with fusion flavors. The taste here is unlike any restaurant I have been to and I look forward to going again. If you plan on going, you have to make your reservation online - you pay upfront and be aware they are open certain days of the week and have seating times. I sat at the bar and loved the view - I got to watch them prepping the dishes and got a little more personal time with the chef. I also loved the interior and secluded entrance. Gosh, even the bathroom was beautiful. Since this was a 10-course meal... I am going to share my top 3 dishes: 1. The Beets & Puri - cashew chutney with beets, greens, and grapefruit. Served with a puri: the puri was cooked perfectly - there was a soft crunch to it and you scooped it into the beets, chutney, etc. The flavor was perfect and refreshing. 2. The Chaas Salad - this buttermilk dressing served with greens was a different twist to one of my favorite drinks at home. The seasoning was perfect. 3. Dal Bhaat - the daal was cooked perfectly and served at the perfect temperature with rice. If you are in the Nashville area, this place is a MUST.

text: We went here on a Friday night at 5:15. We had made reservations for 4 and got our seat right away. We started off by ordering their onion rings (which we had read good things about), and were very underwhelmed. They used a different type of batter, which none of us were a huge fan of. The dinner salads were decent, but there were a few things that left me disappointed. One, we got the exact same serving size of salad and bread that the table of 2 next to us got. Two, the bread was terrible. It was so hard that you couldn't rip it when you took a bite, and the crust was extremely sharp. Our meal itself was okay, but I can tell you it was not at all worth the price we paid for our steaks. My husband got lobster tail and the presentation of it was terrible. It came on a bed of fries, making it completely hard to cut without making a mess. The waitress didn't come back for quite awhile, so we couldn't ask for a side plate to cut it on. Then it came time for dessert. We ordered the wedding cake, because we had also read how amazing it was. Everyone at the table was very underwhelmed by it. The syrup they put around it was way too tart, and the cake itself was very mediocre. The cake came with a scoop of ice cream. What was more frustrating was that we didn't finish our $10 dessert, and so we asked for it to be packed up. After our 60 minute drive home, we realized the gentleman who packaged our dessert, put the ice cream in with it and it was completely melted all over the cake, which we then had to throw away. Honestly, if the place wasn't so overpriced, it would have received a bit of a higher rating from me. However, for the price you are paying, and the experience we left with, I can't give it more than a 1. We will not be returning. I have been to several other steakhouses, paid half the amount, and left feeling much more satisfied then I did here.

The lot is in a L shape extending behind the building. The line to order food was already out the door when I arrived. Again, feeling lucky I didn't have to deal with that mess. I'm not sure if there's an issue that the restaurant was under staffed or in the technology allowed too many ordered in a small window of time but they were extremely backlogged with orders. They were still working on fulfilling the 12:15 pick up when I arrived. How it work is - they have another assembly line set up in the back just to fulfill online order to make it move efficiently rather doing both the mobile orders and in person orders in the same line. I've visited other Omakase style restaurants before (at least 10), all around the same pricing if not more, and I've had a bigger cut of fish on each piece. Some cuts were inconsistent as well. Also, being at a restaurant where the customer can see the chefs make your food, it hurts to see the chefs throw away ends of the fish. It goes against Japanese tradition. Overall, the rice and the fish, the two main/major components of an omakase meal, made my birthday dinner a huge disappointment. I almost always order a la carte after the menu at other omakase restaurants, but this time I didn't. I couldn't even do it for uni, and I LOVE uni; the rice was just too terrible. I was way too excited, this being 5 stars on yelp. Chefs need more training and practice with their cuts; you can see the hesitation. text: I've been coming to Bacchanal quite often since I moved to New Orleans a few years ago. It is a popular spot for locals, especially when it's nice out. It's located in the industrial part of town, away from the tourists of the French Quarter. On Friday and Saturday summer nights, don't be surprised if there's a bit of a line to get in. It usually moves pretty quickly though! Once you enter, you are immediately greeted by a wide variety of wines and cheeses/meats. But don't worry if you're overwhelmed by the selection, there's always someone to help you out if you need assistance finding the best wine, cheese and meats. There's also a good amount of affordable wine options too if you're on a budget. After paying at the counter, they will give you a number to take with you so they can bring your lovely cut cheese/meat platter directly to you. There's a ton of outdoor seating in the back patio. On warmer nights, it can get really packed, so I suggest coming on the earlier side unless you want to spend a bit of time hovering around tables to grab one when it becomes available. On cooler nights, they also have heat lamps available! There's also some indoor seating upstairs which is ideal for the rainier, cooler nights. The outdoor live music is amazing! They have a few different shows throughout the evening; I've never been disappointed by any of the performances. The selection of cheese, meats, and wine is delicious! I've always been happy with the platters I've gotten. They also have some entrees if you want to eat something more substantial. I've never tried any of them, but I've heard they're also quite tasty. Overall, this is a great place to go on a Friday or Saturday evening, if you want something more chill and less crazy than Bourbon Street. Definitely recommend!

text: So many restaurants aspire to be yummy. Defined as pleasing to the senses; especially to the taste; delicious. Yummy House engages all 5 senses, maybe 6, with delectable food and a dining experience that puts this bistro at the top of my list for Chinese food in Tampa. Visually the exterior is nothing to shake a chop stick at, but inside I was greeted by a clean facility with some of the laziest of Susan's center in each table promoting a feeling of togetherness among all groups who come to dine. So many great food options to share, but on this special day I was treated to both pork and pineapple rolls. One savory and one sweet. Bread tender and airy with just the right amount of inner filling to give me an inner filling of joy and satisfaction. Flavors continued to develop as I moved over to the salt and pepper calamari. An absolute must have. We ordered two. Lesser establishments try to pass off second rate squid hidden behind the guise of layers upon layers of greasy batter, but not the yummy house. Fulfilling their delicious promise in name, the calamari was ever so lightly fried bringing forth an excellent balance of salt and spice of pepper alongside the surprise addition of scallions and jalapeños. The main course was the spicy yummy chicken. Found to be ordered by most in my party and for good reason. My friends have excellent opinions on quality food and this yummy chicken was beautifully plated next to two heaping likes of sticky white rices standing like two mountains overlooking flavorful chicken tossed into a lake of a brown yummy sauce swimming alongside sliced mushrooms. Service was prompt and while friendship was the star of the show the food as previously described has landed yummy house on my map of favorite local spots surely to be seen again.

text: I honor of "Transformation Tuesday," I wanted to write a review that is long overdue. Dr. McGuire and her team (Jodi and Rachel) at Parkcrest are literally amazing. I am almost 4 months post-op, time flies when you look great and feel comfortable. Obviously, she is board certified. She is also a decorated doctor who continues to pursue education throughout her career, specifically with regards to gender affirmation surgery. As a queer and trans person, it can be really difficult to find a doctor and team in the Midwest (much less, right here in Saint Louis) who is all of the following: highly skilled in the different types of top surgery, compassionate, confident, aware and sensitive to pronouns and other gender related issues that are relevant when you're getting top surgery. Dr. McGuire knows that different trans and gender non conforming folks who pursue top surgery have different goals with their chest. For me, I was looking for a surgeon who understood that top surgery is more than just removing breast tissue. Dr. McGuire understands that and assured me that she would help masculinize my chest. Trusting someone with your body, and as a trans person trusting someone with the reconstruction of your chest is a huge deal. I am so glad I trusted Dr. McGuire with mine. Her bed side manner is exactly what you'd want in a surgeon: professional, highly confident, with super positive energy. When I left Dr. McGuire's office after my consult, I knew she would be my surgeon. Here's why: It can be easy for such intelligent and skilled people to overlook the importance of sensitivity, especially when it comes to working with folks who are trans. Not only was Dr. McGuire sensitive to my pronouns, but also generally aware of gender dysphoria, which can make going to the doctor, talking about your body, letting others see your body difficult and complicated. Throughout the process my comfort level was a priority. I had great vibes about her from the moment I met her. It's not just her, it's the whole team. Her nurse Rachel is so down to earth and gives amazing care. Jodi, her administrator, is so chill and can somehow make booking appointments and talking about insurance enjoyable. Not only are they outrageously kind and skilled, they are SO efficient. Don't get me wrong, they take their time with you as it's needed, but from the operating room to post op appointments, this team is in and out. They are a well oiled team, obviously communicate well with each other, and they get things done! I am so proud to have had a female surgeon and team for my top surgery. I would choose Dr. McGuire and her team a thousand times over. Thank you, thank you, thank you.

text: We visited the Lafayette Square location about a week ago in the evening and it was surprisingly busy! The windows and interior are very period for the neighborhood with lots of wood and beautiful window script, as well as a cool menu board and cute icecream parlor chairs and tables, although there were only two in the tiny space. I could see this location being hard to navigate in the busy summer months.....but it would be worth every second. They have many different options for icecream combos, some that are not on the board, like single scoops. We all tried the double scoop scenario, which you can get in a cup or cone/waffle cone and mix/match flavors. There are various housemade, made toppings like salted crack crunch bits, hot fudge, house made cherries, etc. as well as drinks, shakes. There are also terrific sounding sundaes, and other combos on the menu board. These would be worth every penny extra I'm sure. They have so many delicious sounding flavors with several seasonal or limited time ones, too. The flavors are divided into "naughty"(alcohol infused) or "nice". The were at least 4 flavors that were vegan/nondairy made with coconut milk too. We tried lots of samples once it was finally our turn to order. I settled on Salted crack caramel and peppermint, which were both some of the most delicious versions I have ever had. My companions had Pistachio, Toffee Butter Brickle, Italian butter cookie, and Decadent coffee. The coffee one wasn't my favorite only because there was a lot of actual crunchy coffee bean bits in there, which I dont care for the texture of, but the flavor was bomb. Omg, all were so flavorful and creamy. They tasted like a pure infusion of their ingredients. You can really taste the quality. Perfect! I dont know how I never tried this place before now, but I dont think I will go anywhere else for icecream in STL.

text: This place is so close to Philly, it's hard to leave Philly thinking there's something better for the vegan gluten-free diet... but then you mosey on over to Heart Beet Kitchen, which I'll call "HBK," and then pa-pow, you're in heaven. This off the beaten path glorious eatery is such a treasure trove of home cooking that you'd hardly have a clue that it was gluten free and vegan! They have desserts, sandwiches, brunch, salads and entrees, as well as beverages like smoothies, and snacks to purchase at the counter. They even have a tote bag and some random items that promote healthful eating. Anyhow, what do you order? Why not order the Heart Beet Burger, a customer favorite, on its own gluten-free bun. It's quite tasty - I love the fresh tomato, avocado and the aioli with the burger. It's nice and moist, good flavor, but not overpowering. I hate when vegan gluten-free burgers are dry or try to mimic meat. This is not that- it's great! The bun though, it's one of the brands I've had before, and it is ok, but not the best, but that's vegan gluten free bread for ya', good enough but not great. Stepping away from traditional sandwiches, I've also had their eggplant meatballs- delicious! Nice flavor and solid, dense, good texture. I have had one other brand of vegan meatballs, as I've never been a fan of the concept of meatballs, but these ones are so good, I would have no qualms ordering them again. Very filling. As a cauliflower addict and aficionado, I loved their cauliflower sandwich. I liked the buffalo cauliflower so much, I am sure that next time I'd skip the sandwich version and order as an appetizer. Then I could order the crab cakes for an entree or the "Philly cheesesteak" with deliciously cooked up mushrooms and a cheesy-like sauce. The stomach can only order so much! The kale salad side is tasty, not too heavy, with a light sesame and orange flavor to the tahini based dressing. When choosing between food and smoothies, it's hard to choose smoothies when I can order all of the food. So, with extra room, what do I order? Cookies, cake, and a cupcake. Again, I am just so happy this place exists, I would order them all! They have coffee cake, too, and tiramisu and raw cookie dough. The cookies and cakes/ cupcakes have good flavor, but they are a little firmer and denser than I would have liked. Still, I can never have dessert that I don't bake, so you better believe every time I am here I will order at least one piece of baked goodness! There's also coffee drinks, lattes of all kinds, and kombucha. This place is my dream come true for casual eating. Loved everything I ordered here, which is a problem, because I can't now think of driving past the Philly/ Cherry Hill area without also building in time to stop here. I am dying to go here for pancakes and waffles, but my waistline will probably be better off not going! Part of me wishes there were some raw entrees and dishes, but, for what this place serves up, I love it.
label: POS

And usually, the overall taste is very underwhelming (especially if you order it without toppings). But Pasqually's stands out for having one of the best-tasting pizza crusts I've had in Philly, and the cheese blend is decent without being overwhelming. Definitely worth it to get a pizza with toppings- not that the ones without are bad, but they mostly do toppings well, so you're missing out with a plain cheese pizza. The vegetable stromboli, even the small, is massive, as everyone else says, and really delicious. Service-wise, they're great for both delivery and takeout. Is it THE BEST pizza in West Philadelphia? text: I've never really been a fan of the Planet Fitness "no judgement zone" marketing, as I find it super hypocritical. That being said, it is an amazing change to come from the Nashville YMCA system that is loaded with Crossfit dudes slamming weights everywhere, to this PF where it's super relaxed. Everyone here goes at their own pace and has no need to compete or show off. The clientele is very diverse, from people that just come in to do cardio or light lifting to people who lift regularly. There are TONS of cardio machines always available, including treadmills, bikes, stairsteppers, ellipticals, and arc trainers. There are 4 smith machines (unfortunately no squat racks), free weight dumbbells, and tons of machines. I've always been able to do full workouts with no wait on any machines because there are so many. Plenty of TVs near the cardio stations, tanning beds, hydro massage beds, and clean locker rooms. They have also added free Wi-Fi since I wrote this first review, and all you need to do to sign in is enter an email address. Also, the staff here is absolutely the best. They've always been super friendly, welcoming, and are always on top of things. All in all, it's a great place to work out, and you can't beat $20 per month ($10 per month if you only plan on working out at this one location. Top that with it being open 24/7, and it's my favorite gym I've ever been a member of.

Line A runs along the side of the home and was the line that appears to have been inspected while line B is the collapsed line that runs to the wall, then meets at a Y with line A and they both run out to the main. When asked about the situation, Sewer-Oscopy stated that line A discharged into B and that when they inspected, water was flowing freely. Unfortunately, that is incorrect and line A does not flow into B and it is presumed Sewer-Oscopy only actually inspected A and not B, at all. All in all they said "they are only responsible for what they see the day of inspection" which, I fully understand, but the problem is they didn't see everything to begin with. I don't believe it was malicious or intentional or anything like that, I think it was just a mistake that they didn't want to take ownership of. I am not one to write negative reviews and, in fact, you can even look at my Yelp history as I can almost always find something positive to say. Homer Plessy, Marie Laveau, Madam LaLaurie (supposedly, but her family, at least), and the future resting place of Nicholas Cage are just a few that most any tour will show you. Here you will see graves that have withstood the test of the past 300 years and you'll learn about how a year and a day is important to all its residents. text: Let me just say this. Some bridal salon stylists try to help you because they care about you and your experience as the bride, while some stylists just want to get paid a commission. David's Bridal needs to work on customer service across the board. They need to figure out a model that makes the customer's experience the most fair it can possibly be, especially given that buying a wedding dress is a huge (and emotional) decision with a huge price tag. I went into David's Bridal feeling very intimidated and unsure of what I was looking for. When faced with an indecisive bride who is just starting out on the dress search, stylists should be advised to approach these situations with special care. If there is any indecision apparent whatsoever, stylists should not be allowed to let that bride pull that credit card out because she feels pressured to buy something after taking up the stylist's time. They should encourage them to think of other ways to become more sure of their decision. Perhaps they could encourage them to come in another day once they've thought about it, not at all making the bride feel rushed, pressured, or bad for not making a decision to purchase that day. Or perhaps they could encourage the bride to order a dress online, since online orders have a 14-day return period (although they wouldn't get a commission in that case). Either way, they should be thinking about the bride and her experience! I recommend that if you are extremely indecisive as I was in the beginning, either order your dress online (like I mentioned before, they give you two weeks to decide whether or not you want to keep the dress) or talk to the store manager about possibly getting at least a few days to change your mind and bring your dress back for a full refund (not just in-store credit). I know they state that there is a no return policy for in-store purchases, but I find this extremely unfair for brides who are just starting out in the dress search and are not really sure what they are looking for or haven't really had much time to process their big-purchase decision. Just mention to the manager that if you are not allowed to get at least a few days to return the dress that you buy in-store (of course, the dress must be in the exact condition it was purchased if you are taking it home from the store) or cancel an in-store order they placed online, you will simply opt to order the dress online yourself. They can make a choice at that point what they are going to do what's best for YOU as the customer (and for their stylists).
